content.comment_body: Hello, I tried using [product_name] to build an easy OEE solution for tracking daily production counts per hour and shift, with visualization in [product_name]. I used UP/DOWN counters and two timers (one for counting, one for reset) for each of the 40 graphs involved. It worked well for a while until an unexpected failure occurred, usually within 1-5 days. After this, all remanent memory was cleared or had random values. Does anyone know what could cause this? Is using 40 counters and 80 timers too much for [product_name]? Can anyone explain the situation? Thanks.
Could it be that [product_name] temporarily enters stop mode?
I haven't seen [product_name] in STOP mode—it remains in RUN mode.
Maybe a temporary power issue is causing it to enter Stop?

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are running into unpredictable data loss and inconsistencies in remanent memory when deploying many counters and timers for production monitoring and visualization using [product_name]. These problems occur sporadically, resulting in deleted or corrupted remanent memory data, even while the system remains in normal operating mode. There is concern over the stability and reliability of [product_name] under high usage conditions, especially during continuous operation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that [product_name] should provide reliable memory retention and stable operation even when managing a high number of counters and timers, without experiencing data loss or memory corruption.
